edges.description: Recessive Chkb loss produces progressive muscular dystrophy.
edges.limitations: Dystrophy follows a rostral-to-caudal gradient set by CHKA expression, and early membrane damage markers are not raised, whereas patients have proximal weakness with raised CK. Intellectual disability and skin findings have not been characterised in the mouse.

edges.description: The rmd mouse shows the same peripheral enlargement and central loss of mitochondria as patient biopsies.
Chkb-null hearts show mitochondrial cristae abnormalities and inefficient electron transport.
edges.limitations: Mice develop cardiac hypertrophy with a smaller left ventricle, not the dilated cardiomyopathy seen in patients.

edges.description: A muscle-specific Chkb transgene, intramuscular AAV6-Chkb after onset, and systemic AAV9 carrying human CHKB each rescue the dystrophic phenotype.
edges.limitations: Preclinical only; no human gene therapy trial has been reported.

nodes.description: Enlarged mitochondria at the fiber periphery with central depletion on oxidative stains and electron microscopy, present in every biopsied patient including the later-onset form.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics of megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to choline kinase beta gene defects in a series of 15 patients.
evidence.snippet: Muscle biopsies were equivocally 'megaconial' in all.

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to CHKB gene variants, the first report of thirteen Iranian patients.
evidence.snippet: Muscle biopsy examination showed the striking finding of peripheral arrangements of large mitochondria in muscle fibers and central sarcoplasmic areas devoid of mitochondria.

nodes.description: Conduction and rhythm abnormalities, including atrial flutter, complete right bundle branch block and left anterior fascicular block, in patients with cardiomyopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Novel CMR findings in megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Electrocardiogram displayed atrial flutter and right bundle-branch block.

evidence.reference_title: A rare homozygous variant of CHKB induced severe cardiomyopathy and a cardiac conduction disorder: a case report.
evidence.snippet: a left anterior fascicular block, and a complete right bundle branch block

evidence.reference_title: A congenital muscular dystrophy with mitochondrial structural abnormalities caused by defective de novo phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: we have identified homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the gene encoding choline kinase beta (CHKB)

evidence.reference_title: Preclinical efficacy of a gene therapy for CHKB-mediated muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: All cases of CHKB-mediated disease are due to a known (or presumed) loss of CHKB enzyme activity.

evidence.reference_title: Alternative splicing events of three rare variants in CHKB gene causing megaconial congenital dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: The c.581G > A variant, instead to produce a missense change (p.Arg194Gln), induces an aberrant splicing event resulting in the deletion of exon 4 (V1 and V2: r.448_581del).

evidence.reference_title: Large heterozygous deletion and uniparental disomy masquerading as homozygosity in CHKB gene.
evidence.snippet: Quantitative PCR revealed that patient 1 had a large deletion encompassing the CHKB gene, inherited from the mother. Single nucleotide polymorphism analysis revealed patient 2 had paternal uniparental isodisomy containing the CHKB gene.

nodes.description: Biallelic nonsense, frameshift, splice-site and missense CHKB variants abolish or reduce choline kinase beta activity. In muscle of patients with nonsense variants choline kinase activity was undetectable.

evidence.reference_title: A congenital muscular dystrophy with mitochondrial structural abnormalities caused by defective de novo phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: In muscle of three affected individuals with nonsense mutations, choline kinase activities were undetectable, and phosphatidylcholine levels were decreased.

evidence.reference_title: Muscular dystrophy with large mitochondria associated with mutations in the CHKB gene in three British patients: extending the clinical and pathological phenotype.
evidence.snippet: CHKB activity was reduced in all three patients and complex 1 activity was significantly reduced in one patient.

evidence.reference_title: A rostrocaudal muscular dystrophy caused by a defect in choline kinase beta, the first enzyme in phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: The rmd mutation is a 1.6-kb intragenic deletion within the choline kinase beta (Chkb) gene, resulting in a complete loss of CHKB protein and enzymatic activity.

nodes.description: Chkb-deficient mouse hearts, including heterozygotes, have reduced atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), its receptor NPRA and ventricular conduction system markers, and are prone to induced arrhythmia. Patients show atrial flutter, bundle branch and fascicular block.

evidence.reference_title: A mouse model of inherited choline kinase β-deficiency presents with specific cardiac abnormalities and a predisposition to arrhythmia.
evidence.snippet: Decreased Chkb level results in a decrease in the levels of regulators and biomarkers for dilated cardiomyopathy and the development of the VCS.

nodes.description: Patient heart muscle shows the same enlarged mitochondria and OXPHOS assembly defect as skeletal muscle. Chkb-deficient mouse hearts accumulate acylcarnitine, a sign that mitochondria cannot use fatty acids, and have mitochondria with abnormal cristae and inefficient electron transport.

animal_models.description: Chkb-null hearts show mitochondrial cristae abnormalities and inefficient electron transport.
animal_models.name: Chkb-null rostrocaudal muscular dystrophy (rmd) mouse

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial muscular dystrophy caused by mitochondrial membrane homeostasis defect, new insights from skeletal and heart muscle analyses.
evidence.snippet: Microscopic evaluation of skeletal and heart muscles typically showed enlarged mitochondria.

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial muscular dystrophy caused by mitochondrial membrane homeostasis defect, new insights from skeletal and heart muscle analyses.
evidence.snippet: Using BN-PAGE analysis followed by activity staining subcomplexes of complex V were detected in both tissues, indicating incomplete complex V assembly.

evidence.reference_title: A mouse model of inherited choline kinase β-deficiency presents with specific cardiac abnormalities and a predisposition to arrhythmia.
evidence.snippet: An increase in acylcarnitine level is also associated with a defect in the ability of mitochondria to use fatty acids for energy and we observed that mitochondria from Chkb-/- hearts had abnormal cristae and inefficient electron transport chain activity.

nodes.description: Used in one adolescent with dilated cardiomyopathy and conduction block (prolonged QRS with left anterior fascicular and complete right bundle branch block); the cardiac outcome of resynchronization was not reported.

evidence.reference_title: A rare homozygous variant of CHKB induced severe cardiomyopathy and a cardiac conduction disorder: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) was provided to the patient due to a prolonged QRS interval (165 ms) with a left anterior fascicular block and complete right bundle branch block.

nodes.description: Spontaneous recessive Chkb null with rapidly progressive hindlimb muscular dystrophy, neonatal forelimb bone deformity, megaconial mitochondria and mitophagy in affected muscle, and cardiac hypertrophy with arrhythmia susceptibility. Forelimb muscle, rich in CHKA, is largely spared.
Speech delay in all children with the congenital form; some never speak.

evidence.reference_title: CHKB-Related Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: All affected children have developmental delay and speech delay

nodes.description: Dilated cardiomyopathy in about a third of children with the congenital form, the main cause of death; one patient underwent heart transplantation. Not reported in the later-onset form.

evidence.reference_title: CHKB-Related Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Dilated cardiomyopathy, seen in 14 children, resulted in death from heart failure in five and cardiac transplantation in one.

evidence.reference_title: A new congenital muscular dystrophy with mitochondrial structural abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: The disease was slowly progressive and 1 patient died from dilated cardiomyopathy at the age of 13 years.

nodes.description: Serum CK is usually mildly to moderately raised.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics of megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to choline kinase beta gene defects in a series of 15 patients.
evidence.snippet: ichthyosis-like skin changes (n = 11), increased serum CK levels (n = 12), microcephaly (n = 6)

nodes.description: Hypotonia from birth or infancy in the congenital presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Novel CHKB mutation expands the megaconial muscular dystrophy phenotype.
evidence.snippet: The patient presented with limb-girdle weakness and hypotonia from birth with mental retardation

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy secondary to novel CHKB mutations resemble atypical Rett syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In addition, generalized hypotonia was a common initial finding.

nodes.description: Developmental delay, most marked in gross motor and language domains, in all children with the congenital form.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics of megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to choline kinase beta gene defects in a series of 15 patients.
evidence.snippet: Core clinical phenotype included global developmental delay prominent in gross-motor and language domains, severe intellectual disability (ID), and/or muscle weakness in all cases.

nodes.description: Heart transplantation has been performed for end-stage dilated cardiomyopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial muscular dystrophy caused by mitochondrial membrane homeostasis defect, new insights from skeletal and heart muscle analyses.
evidence.snippet: This study describes a patient presenting with the cardinal clinical features, in whom a homozygous nonsense mutation (c.248_249insT; p.Arg84Profs*209) was identified in CHKB and who was treated by heart transplantation.

nodes.description: Ichthyosis-like dry scaling skin, often pruritic and sometimes with nummular eczema; a useful clinical clue that distinguishes this from other congenital muscular dystrophies. Its mechanism is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics of megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to choline kinase beta gene defects in a series of 15 patients.
evidence.snippet: ichthyosis-like skin changes (n = 11), increased serum CK levels (n = 12), microcephaly (n = 6)

evidence.reference_title: Importance of Skin Changes in the Differential Diagnosis of Congenital Muscular Dystrophies.
evidence.snippet: Ichthyosis-like skin changes with intense pruritus and nummular eczema may lead to clinical diagnosis in cases with megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: CHKB-Related Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Seizures are seen in some individuals. Ichthyosis is common.

nodes.description: Loss of the first Kennedy-pathway step lowers phosphocholine and impairs phosphatidylcholine synthesis in muscle where CHKB is the dominant isoform, while phospholipase-mediated PC catabolism rises. Whether bulk PC falls is disputed: it was decreased in patient muscle and rmd mitochondria, but a later time-course in Chkb knockout mice found no significant change at any disease stage. Muscle groups rich in the paralog CHKA are spared in mouse.

evidence.reference_title: A congenital muscular dystrophy with mitochondrial structural abnormalities caused by defective de novo phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: In muscle of three affected individuals with nonsense mutations, choline kinase activities were undetectable, and phosphatidylcholine levels were decreased.

evidence.reference_title: Understanding the muscular dystrophy caused by deletion of choline kinase beta in mice.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that the hindlimb muscular dystrophy in Chkb -/- mice is due to attenuated PC biosynthesis and enhanced catabolism of PC.

evidence.reference_title: Differential expression of choline kinase isoforms in skeletal muscle explains the phenotypic variability in the rostrocaudal muscular dystrophy mouse.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that the relative lack of muscle degeneration in forelimbs of Chkb(-/-) mice is due to abundant choline kinase alpha and the stable homeostasis of phosphatidylcholine.

nodes.description: In Chkb knockout muscle, fatty acids cannot be used for energy through mitochondrial beta-oxidation and are shunted into triacylglycerol, with decreased PPAR and target gene expression; PPAR agonists restore beta-oxidation, raise CHKA expression and prevent injury in cultured Chkb-null myocytes. The heart of Chkb-deficient mice shows the same signature as acylcarnitine accumulation.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanism of action and therapeutic route for a muscular dystrophy caused by a genetic defect in lipid metabolism.
evidence.snippet: There is a decrease in peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors and target gene expression specific to Chkb-/- affected muscle.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanism of action and therapeutic route for a muscular dystrophy caused by a genetic defect in lipid metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Treatment of Chkb-/- myocytes with peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonists enables fatty acids to be used for β-oxidation and prevents triacyglyerol accumulation

nodes.description: Defective mitochondria are selectively removed by autophagy, with Parkin, PINK1, LC3, polyubiquitin and p62 localising to mitochondria, and mitochondrial number and mtDNA copy number fall.

evidence.reference_title: Muscle choline kinase beta defect causes mitochondrial dysfunction and increased mitophagy.
evidence.snippet: Molecular markers of mitophagy, including Parkin, PINK1, LC3, polyubiquitin and p62, were localized to mitochondria of rmd muscle.

evidence.reference_title: Phospholipid synthetic defect and mitophagy in muscle disease.
evidence.snippet: Our discovery demonstrates that a phosphatydilcholine biosynthetic defect leads to mitochondrial dysfunction and increased mitophagy.

nodes.description: Intellectual disability of variable severity in most children with the congenital form; cognition is normal or mildly impaired in the later-onset form.

evidence.reference_title: CHKB-Related Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Most have intellectual disability of varying severity; some have no speech.

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to CHKB gene variants, the first report of thirteen Iranian patients.
evidence.snippet: The most common symptoms and signs included intellectual disability, delayed gross-motor developmental milestones, language skills problems, muscle weakness, as well as autistic features, and behavioral problems.

nodes.description: Gross motor milestones are delayed and ambulation is lost over time in the congenital presentation.

evidence.reference_title: CHKB-Related Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: gross motor milestones are delayed with subsequent loss of ambulation over time

nodes.description: The diagnostic biopsy pattern: mitochondria are absent from the center of muscle fibers and markedly enlarged, with complicated cristae, at the periphery. The same pattern is present in rmd hindlimb muscle and in heart muscle of a transplanted patient.

animal_models.description: The rmd mouse shows the same peripheral enlargement and central loss of mitochondria as patient biopsies.
animal_models.name: Chkb-null rostrocaudal muscular dystrophy (rmd) mouse

evidence.reference_title: A new congenital muscular dystrophy with mitochondrial structural abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: Mitochondria at the periphery of fibers were markedly enlarged ("megaconial" appearance) with complicated cristae, and contained a normal amount of mitochondrial DNA by in situ hybridization.

evidence.reference_title: Muscle choline kinase beta defect causes mitochondrial dysfunction and increased mitophagy.
evidence.snippet: No mitochondria were found in the center of muscle fibers, while those located at the periphery of the fibers were significantly enlarged.

nodes.description: Muscle mitochondria of the rmd mouse contain less phosphatidylcholine, the main phospholipid of the inner mitochondrial membrane. An abnormal inner membrane lipid profile is the proposed reason for the respiratory chain defects; whether muscle PC falls at all is disputed (see the edge into this node).

evidence.reference_title: Muscle choline kinase beta defect causes mitochondrial dysfunction and increased mitophagy.
evidence.snippet: Muscle mitochondria in rmd mice exhibited significantly decreased PC levels, impaired respiratory chain enzyme activities, decreased mitochondrial ATP synthesis, decreased coenzyme Q and increased superoxide production.

nodes.description: Mitochondria in Chkb-deficient muscle have impaired respiratory chain activity and ATP synthesis, increased superoxide and decreased inner membrane potential. Patient muscle shows COX-deficient fibres, reduced complex I or combined OXPHOS activity, incomplete complex V assembly and, in one child, mtDNA depletion; patient cells show altered membrane potential.

evidence.reference_title: Muscle choline kinase beta defect causes mitochondrial dysfunction and increased mitophagy.
evidence.snippet: Muscle mitochondria in rmd mice exhibited significantly decreased PC levels, impaired respiratory chain enzyme activities, decreased mitochondrial ATP synthesis, decreased coenzyme Q and increased superoxide production.

evidence.reference_title: Understanding the muscular dystrophy caused by deletion of choline kinase beta in mice.
evidence.snippet: The mitochondria in Chkb -/- mice are abnormally large and exhibit decreased inner membrane potential.

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial muscular dystrophy caused by mitochondrial membrane homeostasis defect, new insights from skeletal and heart muscle analyses.
evidence.snippet: Using BN-PAGE analysis followed by activity staining subcomplexes of complex V were detected in both tissues, indicating incomplete complex V assembly.

evidence.reference_title: Alteration of mitochondrial membrane inner potential in three Italian patients with megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy carrying new mutations in CHKB gene.
evidence.snippet: Here we described an alteration of mitochondrial inner membrane potential and mitochondrial network in cells derived from Italian patients carrying three novel mutations in CHKB gene

evidence.reference_title: Exome sequencing identifies a CHKB mutation in Spanish patient with megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy and mtDNA depletion.
evidence.snippet: Our data confirm the role of CHKB in MDCMC and point to this gene as unique candidate for the combined deficiency of respiratory chain and mtDNA depletion observed in this patient.

nodes.description: Uneven oxidative staining, COX-deficient fibres and reduced complex I or combined complex I, III and IV activity in some patients; one child also had mtDNA depletion.

evidence.reference_title: Muscular dystrophy with large mitochondria associated with mutations in the CHKB gene in three British patients: extending the clinical and pathological phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Muscle pathology showed either myopathic or dystrophic features, uneven oxidative enzyme staining, COX deficient fibres and peripherally located large mitochondria.

evidence.reference_title: Exome sequencing identifies a CHKB mutation in Spanish patient with megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy and mtDNA depletion.
evidence.snippet: enlarged mitochondria in the periphery of the fibers, combined deficiency of complex I, III and IV and depletion of mtDNA

nodes.description: Early-onset dystrophic myopathy with necrosis and regeneration, progressive in most patients.

evidence.reference_title: A congenital muscular dystrophy with mitochondrial structural abnormalities caused by defective de novo phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: We examined 15 individuals with a congenital muscular dystrophy characterized by early-onset muscle wasting, mental retardation, and peculiar enlarged mitochondria

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics of megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to choline kinase beta gene defects in a series of 15 patients.
evidence.snippet: Evolution was progressive (n = 13) and static (n = 2).

nodes.description: Dystrophic changes with necrosis and regeneration, myofiber atrophy and elevated serum creatine kinase. Regeneration after injury is impaired in Chkb-null hindlimb muscle.

animal_models.description: Recessive Chkb loss produces progressive muscular dystrophy.
animal_models.name: Chkb-null rostrocaudal muscular dystrophy (rmd) mouse

animal_models.description: A muscle-specific Chkb transgene, intramuscular AAV6-Chkb after onset, and systemic AAV9 carrying human CHKB each rescue the dystrophic phenotype.
animal_models.name: Chkb-null rostrocaudal muscular dystrophy (rmd) mouse

evidence.reference_title: A new congenital muscular dystrophy with mitochondrial structural abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: In addition to dystrophic changes with necrosis and regeneration in muscle, the most striking finding was mitochondrial depletion in the center of the sarcoplasm.

evidence.reference_title: Preclinical efficacy of a gene therapy for CHKB-mediated muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Chkb -/- mice recapitulate the human disease with affected skeletal muscle displaying a decrease in strength, myofiber atrophy, megaconial mitochondria, fat accumulation within muscle cells, and an increase in muscle injury.

evidence.reference_title: Understanding the muscular dystrophy caused by deletion of choline kinase beta in mice.
evidence.snippet: However, regeneration of hindlimb muscles of Chkb -/- mice was impaired when challenged with cardiotoxin.

nodes.description: Physical therapy to maintain mobility as part of supportive care.

evidence.reference_title: CHKB-Related Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: multidisciplinary care by specialists in pediatric neurology, orthopedics, physical therapy, occupational therapy

nodes.description: Limb-girdle weakness; mild and non-progressive in the later-onset form. Strength can deteriorate transiently with intercurrent illness.

evidence.reference_title: Importance of Skin Changes in the Differential Diagnosis of Congenital Muscular Dystrophies.
evidence.snippet: Physical examination revealed proximal muscle weakness, contractures in the knee of elder sibling, diffuse mild generalized muscle atrophy, and dry skin with ichthyosis together with multiple nummular eczema in both siblings.

evidence.reference_title: Proximal myopathy with focal depletion of mitochondria and megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy are allelic conditions caused by mutations in CHKB.
evidence.snippet: These siblings, aged 37 and 40, are cognitively normal with mild non-progressive muscle weakness and a susceptibility to rhabdomyolysis.

evidence.reference_title: Novel CHKB mutation expands the megaconial muscular dystrophy phenotype.
evidence.snippet: had sudden and transient deteriorations of muscle strength with acute intercurrent illnesses

nodes.description: Brain MRI is structurally normal, but proton spectroscopy shows reduced choline to N-acetylaspartate and choline to creatine ratios in some patients, consistent with less choline and phosphocholine substrate. How this produces intellectual disability is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Muscular dystrophy with large mitochondria associated with mutations in the CHKB gene in three British patients: extending the clinical and pathological phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Brain imaging showed no structural changes but brain magnetic resonance proton spectroscopy (MRS) demonstrated significant reduction in choline:N-acetyl aspartate and choline:creatine ratios in keeping with a general decrease in the amount of choline and phosphocholine-based substrate.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics of megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to choline kinase beta gene defects in a series of 15 patients.
evidence.snippet: Ten patients had cranial neuroimaging (MRI-MRS) study, which was notably normal in all, other than one patient having a decreased choline: creatine peak.

nodes.description: Primary skeletal muscle cells and muscle sections from patients have reduced DRP1, MFF and FIS1, with a disrupted mitochondrial network and lower ATP and Krebs cycle intermediates, offering a second route to enlarged mitochondria.

evidence.reference_title: Reduced mitochondrial fission and impaired energy metabolism in human primary skeletal muscle cells of Megaconial Congenital Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: The expression levels of mitochondrial fission proteins (DRP1, MFF, FIS1) were found to be decreased significantly in both primary skeletal muscle cells and tissue sections of Megaconial CMD by Western blotting and/or immunofluorescence analysis.

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy due to novel CHKB variants: a case report and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Biochemical studies showed reduced levels of the mitochondrial fission factor DRP1 and the severe impairment of mitochondrial respiratory chain activity in patient's muscle compared to controls.

nodes.description: Episodes of rhabdomyolysis and a lasting susceptibility to it in the later-onset limb-girdle presentation.

evidence.reference_title: CHKB-Related Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Two affected individuals presented with rhabdomyolysis.

evidence.reference_title: Proximal myopathy with focal depletion of mitochondria and megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy are allelic conditions caused by mutations in CHKB.
evidence.snippet: These siblings, aged 37 and 40, are cognitively normal with mild non-progressive muscle weakness and a susceptibility to rhabdomyolysis.

nodes.description: In affected Chkb knockout muscle the alpha7beta1 integrin complex fails, with reduced sarcolemmal vinculin, alpha-actinin and actin; choline kinase inhibition in cells internalises PI(4,5)P2 from plasma membrane clusters and removes vinculin from focal adhesions, rescued by CHKB overexpression.

evidence.reference_title: Defects in integrin complex formation promote CHKB-mediated muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: We observed that in Chkb -/- hindlimb muscles there is a decrease in sarcolemma association/abundance of the PI(4,5)P2 binding integrin complex proteins vinculin, and α-actinin, and a decrease in actin association with the sarcolemma.

nodes.description: Early-onset muscle wasting, generalized and usually mild.

evidence.reference_title: A congenital muscular dystrophy with mitochondrial structural abnormalities caused by defective de novo phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: We examined 15 individuals with a congenital muscular dystrophy characterized by early-onset muscle wasting, mental retardation, and peculiar enlarged mitochondria

evidence.reference_title: Importance of Skin Changes in the Differential Diagnosis of Congenital Muscular Dystrophies.
evidence.snippet: Physical examination revealed proximal muscle weakness, contractures in the knee of elder sibling, diffuse mild generalized muscle atrophy, and dry skin with ichthyosis together with multiple nummular eczema in both siblings.

nodes.description: One patient with diffuse ichthyosis-like scaling responded to the IL-12/IL-23 antibody ustekinumab (single case report).

evidence.reference_title: Megaconial congenital muscular dystrophy: Importance of cutaneous features and successful response to ustekinumab.
evidence.snippet: We report a patient with MCMD who had diffuse ichthyosis-like scaling, and successfully responded to ustekinumab.
